source.title: Abhinavagupta's crystal argument already addresses Buddhist self-awareness theory
source.author: Codex/Hermes loop

source_span.quote: Without vimarśa, consciousness would be insentient, like a crystal

claims.claim_text: Abhinavagupta's crystal argument — that without vimarśa consciousness would be insentient like a crystal — applies to any account where self-awareness is derivative rather than intrinsic. The Buddhist phala-model makes self-awareness a result of cognition: if cognition produces self-awareness, then before cognition there is no self-awareness, leaving consciousness insentient. The crystal argument refutes this by showing that consciousness cannot be insentient at any moment, therefore self-awareness must be intrinsic (svabhāva), not produced (phala).
claims.hetu: if self-awareness is produced by cognition, then before cognition there is no self-awareness
claims.sadhya: the crystal argument refutes any derivative account of self-awareness, including svasaṃvitti phala-model
claims.vyapti_statement: If consciousness cannot be insentient at any moment, self-awareness must be intrinsic, not produced.

falsifier.condition: Show that the Buddhist phala-model does not imply periods without self-awareness — i.e., that cognition is continuous and self-awareness is co-extensive with it, making the result-as-nature distinction merely verbal.
